narratives.Description: bug(hooks): the root-mismatch refusal blocks its own named recovery, so a worktree session is locked out (#6594 fix 1)
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

A root-mismatch hook refusal blocks its own named recovery, so a session that hits it is locked out. Admit the refusal's own recovery commands, the same way #6313 did for the pin-mismatch refusal.

Split from #6594 (fix 1 of 3). Fix 2, guarded admission of same-repository linked worktrees, waits on the #6550 direction. Fix 3 is the AGENTS.md lockout note for every host.

## Evidence

Reproduced on 0.129.14 (#6594 comment 6965780737). With the hook running from the primary checkout and the payload `cwd` in a linked worktree, `packages/runtime/src/hook-dispatch.ts` (root check, about line 419) denies every `tool.before` call, including a read-only `git status` and every `deft` / `directive` command. The recovery the refusal prints cannot run from inside that session.

Precedent: the pin-mismatch refusal admits its own named recovery through `pinMismatchRecoveryAdmit` / `admitPinMismatchRecovery` (#6313).

## Proposed change

In the root-mismatch branch of `hook-dispatch.ts`, before rendering the deny, admit a shell `tool.before` call when its command is exactly one of the recovery commands the refusal names, and nothing else is chained to it. Everything else stays refused.

- Admitted set (exact match, no chaining): the read-only diagnostics `directive --version`, `deft --version` and `directive doctor`, plus the disable verb for the session's own host, `directive policy:disable-host-hooks --host <this host> --confirm` (also its `deft` form).
- The refusal text names those commands, and says that the disable takes effect in a new session.
- The foreign-runtime-link branch (#6185) keeps refusing everything; it is out of scope.
- No setup, no policy dispatch, and no occupancy work on the admitted path, as in #6313.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Under a root mismatch, each admitted command is allowed for hosts claude, cursor, grok and codex, and the decision message names the admission.
- [ ] Under a root mismatch, a chained or extended form (`directive doctor && rm x`, `directive doctor; ...`, a pipe or redirect), any other command and any non-shell tool are refused.
- [ ] The refusal text lists the admitted commands.
- [ ] With no mismatch, behaviour is unchanged (existing hook-dispatch tests pass).
- [ ] No new default refusal is added, so the #6281 warn-first table is not touched (if review finds otherwise, declare it there).

## Out of scope

Admitting linked worktrees (fix 2), deposit or installer changes, general read-only shell, and MCP or browser tools.

arc or design-critique: not warranted, because this mirrors the shipped #6313 admission pattern on one more refusal, with an exact-match allowlist and no new policy.
